Source: https://thehackernews.com/2026/10/qilin-and-inc-ransomware-groups-exploit.html
Primary: https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/active-exploitation-of-pan-os-cve-2026-0257/

The concrete behaviors are disabling ESXi execInstalledOnly and extracting
credentials offline from a domain-controller VMDK. No VPN exploit or custom
binary was supplied. Reconstruction tools are not attributed to the actor.

Placement and detection changes:
- Move ESXi execution-policy disabling from impact/ransom/esxi to
  evasion/security-bypass/policy/execution. Same-command setting/value patterns
  replace loose command + path + unrelated -i 0 proximity. Add reversed runtime
  flag order, boot-kernel control, and encryption-policy requirement variants.
- Move esxcli advanced-setting modification and execution-control path references
  to micro-behaviors/os/virtualization/hypervisor; preserve their original scope.
- Retire esxcli-i-zero-flag: a bare -i 0 is neither ESXi-specific nor a useful
  standalone observation. Its complete disabling commands retain coverage.
- Move esxcli-tool from os/sysinfo/vmware to os/virtualization/hypervisor and
  update its six exact references. Preserve matcher, criticality and scope.
  No ancestor-directory consumers of the moved neutral observations exist.
- Require an actual download call's first string argument to name NTDS.dit.
  This targeted acquisition belongs in credential-access/files/password-database,
  and remains suspicious because legitimate forensic acquisition is possible.

The synthesized sample is classified suspicious and must fire both policy
bypass and NTDS acquisition. It uses runtime policy disabling and read-only
VMDK extraction, then offline NTDS parsing. The new rule does not claim decryption
from a download alone. Neither Qilin nor INC identity is inferred from common
behaviors. Do not force a hostile verdict for legitimate dual-use operations.

Positive and near-miss controls:
  cleave/tests/fixtures/esxi-ntds-controls/variant.rb
    boot policy disable + NTDS download: both suspicious behaviors
  cleave/tests/fixtures/esxi-ntds-controls/variant.sh
    reversed runtime flags + encryption requirement false: both match
  cleave/tests/fixtures/esxi-ntds-controls/benign_admin.py
    queries, enabling, unrelated zero setting, comments, unrelated source with
    NTDS as destination, and NTDS.dit.txt: no new suspicious findings
  cleave/tests/fixtures/esxi-ntds-controls/benign_split_commands.sh
    a setting and a value on distinct commands: no policy-disable finding

The original and replacement ESXi matchers are text observations, not proof of
execution; literal command text in documentation can still match. The credential
rule uses structured call arguments and does not match prose or comments.
Exact invocation records, facts, indicator provenance and scan output are in
scratch/threat-feed/3950 outside the sample directory. SHA256/PURLS are empty:
no actor hashes or malicious package coordinates are provided. Primary-report
IP addresses and spoofable client names are kept separate from sample identity.
